GRILL.means: interview the user, one question at a time, to settle decisions before anything is built

PLAN.means: write a plan, a spec or tickets

RESEARCH.means: look up facts outside the session (the web, docs, other repositories) to answer a question or prepare a decision

EXECUTE.means: make the change, build it, do the task

DEBUG.means: find out why something is broken or failing

REVIEW.means: judge something already written: code, a plan, a pull request

EXPLAIN.means: answer a question or teach, changing nothing

NOTE.means: turn a source (a page, a video, a document) into notes in the vault, or write the daily log

LAND.means: commit, push, open or merge the pull request of finished work

CLEAN.means: tidy branches, worktrees, the environment or running processes

machine: Another Claude session sent a message

model.name: haiku
ask: You label what a coding agent will do next, from the end of its last message to the user and the user's new prompt.
Reply with exactly one word, one of:
KEEP: the agent goes on with what its current label says, or the prompt asks for nothing (a thank-you, a remark).
Label the work the prompt sets off, not its wording.

A short answer to a question the agent asked (a number, a letter, a yes or a no, a choice) is KEEP: the same work goes on. The exception is an answer that starts other work: a yes, a go-ahead or a confirmation of the agent's plan, summary of decisions or offer to build, change or fix something is EXECUTE; an approval to push or merge finished work is LAND.

Feedback or a correction on what the agent delivered, asking for changes, is EXECUTE. A question that wants an explanation and no change is EXPLAIN; a report that something is broken, or a question why it fails, is DEBUG.
